title: Causal rebase receipt
description: Completed causal rebase summary with plan identity, omissions, applications, recreated merges, trees, and timing, attached to the rebased tip (shared-portable note record; src/rebase-operations.js finalizeRebase). A strict superset of v1: v2 adds `recreatedMerges`, which a merge-preserving rewrite fills and a linear one leaves empty (ADR-0034).

proof.description: Coverage proof, or null for new work: commit-ancestry, receipt-commit, stable-change-id, receipt-change-id, git-patch-id-heuristic. Records written before v0.12.0 may carry signed-shaped-landing-receipt where receipt-commit now appears; nothing branches on the value, so readers pass it through unchanged (docs/schemas/compatibility.md).

Coverage proof, or null for new work: commit-ancestry, receipt-commit, stable-change-id, receipt-change-id, git-patch-id-heuristic. Records written before v0.12.0 may carry signed-shaped-landing-receipt where receipt-commit now appears; nothing branches on the value, so readers pass it through unchanged (docs/schemas/compatibility.md).

resultCommit.description: The commit this record is attached to; when the record carries attachedTo, both must be equal.

timings.description: Pre-publication operation measurements, not whole-command telemetry. See docs/schemas/receipt-timings.md for the distinct measurement boundaries.

activeApplicationMs.description: Accumulated active application spans, including successful continuation setup, excluding user pause time and finalization/publication.

elapsedWallMs.description: Wall time from operation.startedAt to receipt construction before publication, including time paused between invocations; not end-to-end command latency.

git.description: Accumulated Git metric scopes inside application-queue calls. Excludes planning, continuation work before queue entry, finalization, record/provenance publication, and journal cleanup. Null means unavailable, not zero cost.

quarantinedFacts.description: Identifiers reachable from the target that the conflict rule excluded, so a reviewer can see that coverage was computed on reduced evidence (ADR-0030). Absent in records written before v0.15.0; an empty array means nothing was excluded. Deliberately outside every plan fingerprint.

range.description: The source set this plan describes. Without --from, `base` is the physical merge base and `explicit` is false, so a v1 plan is unchanged. The plan fingerprint covers `base`, because it decides what would be replayed; it does not cover `explicit`, because naming the same base is the same range (ADR-0032). Absent in records written before v0.15.0.

baseRef.description: The revision the caller named, as typed, or null when the base was implicit.

excludedByRange.description: Commits between the physical merge base and the range base: work the caller declared out of the source set. They are listed and nothing else — never replayed, classified, absorbed, or covered, and no receipt claims them. The omission is declared, not proven (ADR-0032).

recreatedMerges.description: The merges this rewrite recreated, in the order it recreated them. A recreated merge is a join, not a contribution: it claims nothing about the changes beneath it, and a plan may conclude nothing from this entry. It is not exact evidence under ADR-0004, it contributes to no coverage class, and `vlab merge-plan` must not count it as covering anything. The entry exists so a reader can audit what the rewrite did to the topology and so provenance can be carried onto the new object (ADR-0034). Empty for a linear rewrite; absent in records written before v0.17.0, which were always linear.

originCommit.description: The merge that was recreated. It is never in absorbedCommits: a receipt that absorbed a join would be claiming the work beneath it.

originChangeId.description: The original merge's identity, or `git:<commit>` when it carried no Change-Id.

changeId.description: The new join's new identity, which is never the original's. A rebase replaces the parents by construction, so a recreated merge is a different join even when its resolution is byte-identical; preserving the original identity would assert a sameness the operation cannot support, and would be the route by which a rewrite could inflate coverage (ADR-0034).

parents.description: The rewritten parents, in order, each mapped to the original parent it replaces. v1 topology is two parents, both in the rebased range or ancestors of the new base; octopus merges and out-of-range parents are refused by name before any mutation.

replaces.description: The original parent this one replaces, or null for a root commit's absent parent.

source.description: `rewritten` when the parent was itself rewritten by this operation; `new-base` when it was outside the range and the new base replaced it.

resolutions.description: The resolution outcomes the join required. Each publishes an ordinary vcs-lab.resolution/v1 record, because it is an ordinary resolution: that a merge rather than a pick produced the conflict changes nothing about its signature (ADR-0034).

origin.description: `exact-reused` when a recorded signature supplied the result, `decided` when a person resolved it during the operation.

cleanJoin.description: True when the merge required no resolution at all.

relation.description: Not an application relation, and must not be counted as one (ADR-0034).
